codeReview.summary: Clean implementation of the edit entity page. Diff computation is correct, form prefill works via triplesToFormData, error states are well-handled (404, generic error, submission failure, polling failure). Edit button correctly gated behind alive status. Route ordering (edit before detail) prevents shadowing. 21 tests cover rendering, diff logic, submission, and error flows. No-op detection works at both form level (disabled button) and handler level (early return).

issues.description:
Test 'navigates back to entity detail on success' asserts the mutation was called but never asserts that navigation actually happened (e.g. screen.getByText('Entity detail')). The test name implies navigation verification (VAL-EDIT-007) but only verifies the mutation payload. The MemoryRouter wrapper has a /entities/:id route that renders
Entity detail
, so asserting that text would be sufficient.

If useEntity returns isError=false and entity=undefined simultaneously (race condition where loading finishes but entity is null), the loading state guard `isLoading || !initialData` catches it. This is correct but the stale closure risk in handleSubmit is worth noting: `initialData` is captured in useCallback's deps and is a useMemo ref, so it should be stable as long as entity doesn't change mid-edit. Acceptable.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker correctly placed the /entities/:id/edit route BEFORE /entities/:id in router.tsx to prevent the :id param from matching 'edit'. This ordering subtlety is not documented in AGENTS.md. Other workers adding nested entity routes (e.g. /entities/:id/relations/new) would benefit from knowing this pattern.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: router.tsx:28-30 — edit route placed before detail route. React Router matches top-down, so 'edit' would be captured as :id if routes were reversed.
